ai.description: This frog reaches 4–8 cm. It is green dorsally with a distinct white upper lip stripe and dark flank mottling. Key features include long, slender limbs and expanded, pale-colored toe discs.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Odorrana chloronota* is the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or lime-green patch on the dorsal skin, absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Odorrana chloronota* inhabits clear, rocky streams within evergreen tropical forests, typically at elevations ranging from 200 to 1,500 meters in the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The Chloronate Huia frog is primarily nocturnal, often perching on rocks near fast-flowing streams where it uses its powerful hind legs to leap into water when threatened.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Odorrana chloronota* is an oviparous species that breeds during the monsoon season, depositing eggs in clusters attached to submerged rocks in fast-flowing hill streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Odorrana chloronota* occurs in Northeast India (e.g., Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya) and the Eastern Himalayas, typically inhabiting streams at elevations of 200–1,500m.
ai.callDescription: The *Odorrana chloronota* produces a high-pitched, rhythmic series of short, melodic whistles, typically heard near fast-flowing streams in forested mountain habitats.
